title: arXiv Trending Physics — latest batch, 1 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred editorial ranking, and the newest papers have little citation history, so it is not a popularity or readership ranking.

sections.title: Drell-Yan lepton pair production from low to high transverse momentum
sections.abstract: The authors present particle-level Drell–Yan predictions combining N3LO fixed-order accuracy, approximate N4LL′ resummation at low-to-moderate transverse momentum, multi-jet precision, and lattice-QCD input for the Collins–Soper kernel.
sections.claimed_result: The authors construct strictly positive event weights that transfer high-precision theory predictions into particle-level simulations; the abstract specifies tree-level accuracy for Z+4–6 jets and approximate NLO electroweak accuracy at high transverse momentum.
sections.evidence_basis: Cross-listed across phenomenology, experiment, and lattice subfields; combines high-order QCD predictions with continuum-limit lattice input, and the HTML paper says the event-weight program is publicly available.
sections.unique_caveat: Precision is regime-dependent, with approximate resummation/electroweak components and tree-level multi-jet accuracy; the paper also fits a non-perturbative width to LHC data.

sections.title: Strongly coupled ultracompressed self-cavity plasmon polaritons at millikelvin temperatures
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate a superconducting self-cavity platform with electromagnetic-volume compression of order 10^7 and observe graphene cavity plasmon polaritons down to 0.04 THz at millikelvin temperatures.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe underdamped graphene cavity plasmon polaritons and avoided crossings in superconducting self-cavities, using a superconducting-circuit sub-THz spectrometer.
sections.evidence_basis: A concrete experimental platform and spectrometer are reported, with avoided crossings between measured plasmon-polariton and cavity modes; the full text identifies simultaneous transport/spectroscopy as a capability to pursue.
sections.unique_caveat: This establishes the measurement platform and hybrid modes, not a cavity-induced change to a material phase; the authors leave correlated transport and cavity response for future work and note model discrepancies tied to coupler-property uncertainty.

sections.title: The star formation history of Orion is structured and episodic
sections.abstract: Using an age map of 47 co-moving Orion groups, the authors find four star-formation peaks roughly 5 Myr apart, with only the two younger peaks robust to resampling and age-fitting changes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer stronger star-formation episodes at 6.4 and 11.3 Myr ago and weaker features near 16.2 and 21.4 Myr, with an approximately 5 Myr spacing also seen in Sco-Cen.
sections.evidence_basis: The paper combines a 47-group age map with explicit resampling and age-model checks; it reports that the two better-supported peaks contain about 59% of the stars and compares the pattern with Scorpius–Centaurus.
sections.unique_caveat: The two older peaks are not robust across resamples; absolute ages depend on isochrone and fitting choices at roughly the 1–3 Myr level, and the paper says the physical cause of the spacing remains unresolved.

sections.title: Inferring radio beams from sparse sampling patterns: a case study with the Murchison Widefield Array
sections.abstract: Reprocessed satellite measurements and two Bayesian models yield repeatable 137-MHz zenith-beam reconstructions for the Murchison Widefield Array, including departures from nominal simulations.
sections.claimed_result: The reconstructed beams show shallower, displaced nulls and coherent sidelobe deformations relative to nominal electromagnetic simulations; the authors find satellite transmissions can support repeatable beam reconstruction.
sections.evidence_basis: The authors compare a dipole-variation model with a hierarchical spline model and report consistent null/sidelobe morphology in four separate 20-day subsets; the work addresses calibration errors relevant to 21-cm cosmology.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated result is a 137-MHz zenith-pointed power beam; the authors identify chromatic and phase-referenced measurements of the full Jones response as follow-up work.

sections.title: How eccentric is the debris disk of epsilon Eridani? ALMA reveals a near-circular belt
sections.abstract: A reanalysis of ALMA Band 6 data places tight limits on the eccentricity of ε Eridani’s debris belt and reports tentative evidence for a small forced eccentricity, while combining the disk fit with Spitzer and JWST data to constrain additional planets.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give upper limits of 2.6% for forced eccentricity and 6.8% for proper eccentricity, alongside a tentative 1.62% forced eccentricity estimate; their combined analysis constrains possible outer planets over roughly 6–60 au.
sections.evidence_basis: The arXiv record says accepted for publication in ApJ; the study reports 99.7th-percentile eccentricity limits and combines ALMA with Spitzer and JWST constraints.
sections.unique_caveat: The nonzero forced eccentricity is explicitly tentative and model-dependent; the limits constrain the disk and allowed architectures rather than detecting an additional planet.

sections.title: Polynomial-time classical and quantum simulation of quantum impurity models
sections.abstract: The authors prove polynomial-time classical algorithms for static impurity-model properties while showing that dynamical quantities can encode problems as hard as general quantum computation.
sections.claimed_result: For the model class studied, the authors give polynomial-time classical estimates of ground-state energy and thermal partition functions, but show nonequilibrium Green’s functions can capture the full power of quantum computation.
sections.evidence_basis: The work bridges quantum information, correlated matter, chemistry, and computational complexity; it sharpens the static-versus-dynamical boundary with stated polynomial guarantees.
sections.unique_caveat: These are complexity guarantees for a defined impurity-model setting, not a benchmark of practical runtimes or evidence of an experimental quantum advantage.

sections.title: Hyperbolic lattices with mass disorder: Phases and phase transitions
sections.abstract: Numerical tight-binding calculations find distinct disorder-driven transitions in three hyperbolic-lattice models, including a Dirac-liquid semimetal-to-metal transition followed by an Anderson transition.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that weak mass disorder leaves the hyperbolic Dirac liquid stable, with a semimetal-to-metal transition at moderate disorder and a metal-to-insulator transition at stronger disorder; the other two models show only the latter transition.
sections.evidence_basis: It is cross-listed across three condensed-matter categories and compares three lattice geometries using average and typical density-of-states calculations with the kernel polynomial method.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions are for idealized nearest-neighbor models with open boundaries; the abstract does not establish these phases in a specific material.

sections.title: Leading gravitational dressing of operators and states in de Sitter space
sections.abstract: At leading nontrivial order in Newton’s constant, the authors construct gravitationally dressed, de Sitter-invariant observables on a time-symmetric slice and test a two-scalar example against linearized Schwarzschild–de Sitter behavior.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show dressability requires the underlying field-theory observable to be de Sitter invariant and explicitly construct the dressing for a two-particle scalar state in the large-mass limit.
sections.evidence_basis: The paper supplies an explicit Green-function construction and an example with a correlator check against a linearized gravitational solution, rather than only proposing a formal framework.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is only to leading nontrivial order in Newton’s constant and is conditional on de Sitter-invariant observables; the authors leave questions about a more complete construction open.

summary.text: More reliable inference from imperfect observations: Orion’s Gaia-based age reconstruction tests whether peaks survive resampling and age-model changes; MWA Bayesian beam inference addresses sparse satellite sampling; ε Eridani combines ALMA and infrared constraints.

Bridging calculations to usable simulation or measurement: Drell–Yan converts high-order theory into positive event weights; the impurity-model paper separates classical tractability of equilibrium properties from quantum-hard dynamics.
New access to coupled light–matter response: the millikelvin graphene/superconducting-cavity experiment demonstrates ultracompressed sub-THz polariton spectroscopy.
The hyperbolic-lattice disorder diagram and de Sitter dressing construction are distinct single-paper signals, not evidence of a broader surge.
Improve coupler characterization and test cavity-induced changes in electronic response using simultaneous transport and spectroscopy.
Test the robustness of Orion’s older peaks and the approximately 5 Myr spacing with better ages for embedded young stars and comparisons across star-forming complexes.
Extend satellite-based MWA beam inference across frequency and direction, including chromatic and phase-referenced full-Jones measurements.
Test ε Eridani’s possible outer-planet architecture with deeper imaging or additional astrometry.
Test the Drell–Yan event-weight results against differential LHC measurements and improved lattice constraints on non-perturbative inputs.
Quantify practical resources for representative nonequilibrium impurity-model calculations and compare classical approximations with quantum algorithms.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The strongest signals are methodological: improved precision and calibration across collider theory, low-temperature spectroscopy, and astronomical inference. Several results remain bounded by model dependence, limited measurement regimes, or systematic uncertainty.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.summary: Daily window: latest batch dated 2026-10-01, with submitted-record timestamps from 2026-09-30 18:00:00 UTC to 2026-10-01 18:00:00 UTC exclusive. One grouped arXiv API query covered physics.*, astro-ph.*, cond-mat.*, gr-qc, hep-ex, hep-lat, hep-ph, hep-th, nucl-ex, nucl-th, and quant-ph; 481 unique eligible papers were returned and cross-lists deduplicated. The top three were additionally inspected in arXiv HTML. Semantic Scholar returned an indexed record for one selected paper, with zero citations; citation momentum therefore did not discriminate this fresh batch.
